posts.content:
Four weeks into my journey at Notion, and the opportunity ahead is even greater than I imagined.

A few early reflections:

A culture of innovation: We are genuinely “customer zero”. We are empowered to build, experiment and lead the way before helping our customers do the same. Its super exciting being here and empowering to see everyone building and learning from one another.

A significant opportunity for businesses of all sizes: After 19 years (wow, I’m old) across consulting, FinTech and RevTech, I’ve seen plenty of technology shifts. This one feels different.

The opportunity is not simply to add AI to existing tools. It is to rethink how teams and AI work together, combining knowledge, workflows and trusted company context to turn intelligence into action.

That is where Notion comes in. It brings knowledge and execution together in one connected, AI-powered workspace, so people and agents can do their best work with context they can trust.

An equally significant opportunity for partners: Customers want to move beyond AI experimentation, but many are struggling with adoption and with designing agentic and human workflows that meaningfully improve how their teams operate.

Every function has workflows ready to be reimagined with context sprawled across multiple systems and silos. 

For Product teams, it might be turning customer feedback into product decisions. For Sales and GTM teams, moving from account research to coordinated execution. For Marketing teams, taking a campaign from brief to launch while keeping people, knowledge and AI connected.

Partners can help close the gap between ambition to reality and I'm so excited about being part of the building journey in this region.

A big big thank you to all the team thats made me feel so welcome. 

Four weeks down. A lot learned. Even more to build.

repost.content:
Ever since offices have existed, they’ve projected a certain image of the companies who build them. And in the tech space, this has usually meant a forward-looking aesthetic—Apple’s spaceship, Amazon’s geodesic domes, and Bell Labs’ mirrored complex. It’s a fitting, and often repeated, conceit for businesses that are designing the future. (Or want to be perceived as such.)  

This pattern is part of the reason why the new San Francisco headquarters of Notion, a productivity software company that pivoted to AI a few years ago, feels unexpected. Designed by IA Interior Architects, the 100,000-square-foot space located in a circa 1907 building expresses a more historic sensibility. To wit: Its lobby is furnished with a book-matched burl reception desk, antique Persian carpets, gauzy white curtains, and an authentic Gerrit Rietveld chair. Noticeably absent? Logos and screens. As Kristoffer Tendall, IIDA, the design director of IA's San Francisco office, told me on a walk-through, these tactile and atmospheric details "celebrate the person who’s here."

It reflect's the interests of the company's founders, which include history and collectible design. “This isn’t a tech office; this is a Notion office,” says Michael McGinley, Notion's head of real estate. “That’s always been [cofounder Ivan Zhao's] philosophy and vision. He wants us to be a place that is dedicated to literature, to poetry, to architecture. That can still exist in an AI company, but it’s the story we tell about ourselves to ourselves, and what inspires us and what we want to think about day-to-day. And I think that is very unique to this space.”

Get the full story in Fast Company. (Big thanks to Judy Nelson and Amelia Salyers for their help with the piece!)

posts.content:
Questions our Notion team heard at the Lenny and Friends Summit in San Francisco yesterday, and how we answered them:

Q: How is Notion evolving and positioning itself nowadays?
A: We've historically been known as a hub for company knowledge, docs, and projects. That matters now more than ever because AI needs the right context to be effective. We want Notion to be the context layer for your teams and agents, so no matter what tools you use or workflows you run, you can bring it all together in one shared workspace.

Q: How do you see organizations really benefitting from using Notion?
A: Notion's value becomes exponential when you consider how many tools it can help your team replace. Notion can become your company's go-to for docs, wikis, meeting notes, project management, and more. Having one place for everything makes teams across the org that much more aligned and productive. And most teams are usually much happier using Notion too :)

Q: What if my team is already comfortable in the tools they’re using and doesn’t want to learn a new tool?
A: Thanks to Notion’s extensibility, whether that’s MCP, APIs, or SDKs, you can work from within Notion or directly in the other tools you care about. Either way, Notion serves as the brain for your organization, and the context layer that powers your team's workflows.

Q: What if I have data that exists outside of Notion? How can Notion be my second brain and context layer if it doesn’t have everything in it?
A: You can bring data into and out of Notion via our developer platform at notion.dev. Notion doesn't need to be your CRM, for example, but it can bring your CRM data into Notion, making that data accessible for your day-to-day work.

Q: What are you all most excited about with upcoming Notion releases?
A: Custom Views! Finally, you can build whatever view you want for your Notion data. Want an Obsidian-style graph view in Notion? Don’t wait for us to build it; you can build it yourself now. Currently in beta!

Huge thank you to the amazing Kevin Tran for helping us synthesize the themes above, to our events wizard Nora Gardner for orchestrating Notion's presence at the summit, and to Lenny Rachitsky for building an amazing community of Product leaders and friends, and inviting us to join!

Notion is rebuilding its go-to-market motion around a workflow-first, builder-led model.
 
Here are some roles we’re hiring for:
 
Solutions Consultant: You’ll own the full customer journey: from first meeting through workflow design, commercial close, workflow implementation, expansion & renewal planning. You are the single owner of your accounts, accountable for ensuring what you sell actually gets realized. You’ll build live in front of customers, translate workflow designs into commercial outcomes, and be a trusted partner with genuine continuity across the entire relationship. If you’re a builder who loves to sell and you want to work at the intersection of AI, productivity, and enterprise then this is the role for you.
 
Business Development Rep: You'll be the force that turns the right accounts into the right conversations. You'll partner closely with Solutions Consultants to identify and target companies that are ready to rethink how they work, and your job is to get them in the room. This isn't generic pipeline work: you're qualifying for workflow-first, build-ready opportunities that set SCs up to win. If you're competitive, curious, and energised by outbound that actually means something, this is the role for you.
 
Forward Deployed Engineer: You’ll lead the hands on technical delivery of our most complex customer engagements. You will design, build, and deploy production ready solutions that help enterprise customers integrate Notion as the operating layer for their business.  You’ll embed with customers to design and build solutions that integrate Notion deeply into their technical and operational environments.
 
This is a customer-facing engineering role for someone who is comfortable writing code, debugging technical issues, explaining tradeoffs to stakeholders, and turning ambiguous customer problems into scalable technical solutions. Your work will help shape best practices for how we support complex customer needs and ensure Notion’s platform is ready for scale.
 
Outcomes Architect: You’ll be the build-beside partner who helps customers turn AI ambition into working systems inside Notion. You’ll own workflow adoption, value delivery, and renewal outcomes for a book of named accounts, with a focus on customers that are flat, at-risk, or need a stronger path to measurable impact.
 
You’ll partner closely with Solutions Consultants on account strategy, expansion qualification, and planning, while directly shaping outcomes that strengthen customer partnerships and contribute to predictable revenue. If you’re someone who loves helping customers build workflows that solve real business problems and you want to work at the intersection of AI, productivity, customer value, and revenue impact then this is the role for you.

posts.content:
We try to make Notion a little better, each day. Sometimes with big updates. Sometimes with eight tiny things that make your day 2% better.

Here’s 8 tiny things:

1️⃣ 𝗔 𝗺𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝗼𝗿𝗴𝗮𝗻𝗶𝘇𝗲𝗱 𝗺𝗼𝗱𝗲𝗹 𝗽𝗶𝗰𝗸𝗲𝗿

Models are now grouped by provider with Favorites up top. Just star the models you reach for most.

2️⃣ 𝗘𝗳𝗳𝗼𝗿𝘁 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗹𝘀

Tell Notion AI how hard to think before it starts.
For Custom Agents, you’ll find it in Settings → Advanced.
For your Personal Agent, it’s right next to the model picker.

3️⃣ 𝗦𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗮 𝗽𝗮𝗴𝗲 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝗮 𝗖𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗺 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁

Same Share flow as adding a teammate. Pick the agent, give it access, and it can use that page as context.

4️⃣ 𝗖𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝗡𝗼𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝘁𝗼 𝗰𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗮 𝘀𝗸𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝘀𝗰𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗰𝗵

Great prompts tend to live in one person’s head or otherwise disappear into standalone docs and chats. Now they can turn that know-how into a skill and level up the whole team.

5️⃣ 𝗔𝗜 𝗠𝗲𝗲𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗡𝗼𝘁𝗲𝘀 𝗰𝗮𝗻 𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗴𝗲𝗿 𝗮𝗻 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁

When a meeting note is finished, an agent can kick off automatically. So the follow-up can start right after the summary exists: draft a recap, update a project page, prep next steps, whatever your workflow needs.

6️⃣ 𝗘𝗺𝗯𝗲𝗱 𝗮 𝗖𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗺 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗶𝗻 𝗮 𝗽𝗮𝗴𝗲

7️⃣ 𝗖𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗺 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 𝗔𝗣𝗜 𝗶𝘀 𝗻𝗼𝘄 𝗶𝗻 𝗽𝘂𝗯𝗹𝗶𝗰 𝗯𝗲𝘁𝗮

Earlier this year, we introduced Think Together: a manifesto for the future we believe in at Notion. Here's a little BTS on how we built the campaign.
 
At its core, Think Together is about a future where AI helps people accomplish more together, not just alone. This summer, our creative team took that idea to a much bigger stage, expanding it across video and billboards around the world.
 
The idea was simple: take iconic images of human achievement and collaboration and quite literally remove the people behind them. Suddenly, you could feel what was missing.
 
We partnered with the incredible team at Ways & Means to bring that idea to life, with a huge amount of thought and craft behind every detail.
 
We looked at hundreds of images across science, construction, culture, sports to find the moments that made the idea really land. Photos were printed, teammates were physically cut out with an X-Acto knife, and images were scanned back in. Add an original score, the perfect voiceover, lots of editing and iteration, and a simple idea started to become a whole campaign.
 
Then we took it around the world, working closely with our regional teams to rethink the imagery, voice, and execution across eight markets so the idea felt relevant wherever it showed up.
 
Fittingly, the making of Think Together was every bit as collaborative as the idea behind it. So much care and craft came from Rusty Van Riper Huy Vu Sachi Chandiramani Calla Salinger Lila Murphy Cory Zapatka Palmer Taylor Ashley Min Rhona He Ways & Means and so many others.
 
Here’s a little peek at how it all came together ↓ You can check out the full spot on YouTube: https://lnkd.in/gTn6cffb

AI is changing the Customer Success role and at Notion, that evolution has a name: Outcomes Architect.

For years, the CSM role has been about helping customers adopt software, realise value, and build lasting partnerships. That work still matters deeply. But AI has raised the bar. 

Customers don’t just need help understanding features anymore. They need partners who can help them rethink how work gets done.

That means moving from:
💫  Adoption plans → workflow transformation
🏗️ Enablement sessions → build-beside partnerships
✅ Value check-ins → measurable business outcomes
🔀 Product expertise → AI, workflow, and systems design fluency

The Outcomes Architect role is about helping customers turn AI ambition into practical, governed, repeatable systems. Because the real value of AI doesn’t come from using one more tool. It comes from embedding AI into the workflows where teams make decisions, move projects forward, support customers, onboard employees, run reviews, and scale knowledge.

That requires a different kind of customer partner: someone who can diagnose the workflow, understand the customer’s operating model, advise on governance, connect AI usage to measurable value, and help teams build with confidence.

For me, this is the most exciting part of the transition. The future of Customer Success is not just relationship management. It’s not just renewal ownership. And it’s not just product adoption. It’s strategic, technical, AI-enabled partnership — helping customers design better ways of working and prove the impact.

That’s the shift from CSM to Outcomes Architect.

And in an AI-native world, I think it’s exactly where Customer Success needs to go.

posts.content:
Who knew that writing timetables in 3rd grade would lead to my dream internship? 

This summer, I joined Notion as the first Revenue Operations intern. 

Since I was 8, I’ve been writing my daily routine on paper. I have to admit, my parents forced me when I started. 

By high school, I got obssessed w/ testing productivity hacks. But, I ended up getting so stressed out because I couldn’t follow my plan of getting 36 hours of work done in a day…

That’s when I found Notion. I was able to organize everything seamlessly on one page. It looked so sleek that I wasn’t overwhelmed. I could actually make a realistic plan without losing my mind. 

By the time I got to college, my Notion obsession had only grown bigger. Without conscious effort I turned into a Notion evangelist. I showed up to countless dinners, convincing everybody I knew to build pages by showing them my setup.

I even designed my own major to be similar to Ivan’s (one of the co-founders and CEO) who studied Cognitive Systems in college. 

Inspired by Akshay (another co-founder) building companies every quarter during his masters, I decided to do 4 internships during my freshman year to figure out what I cared about. 

At some point, my friends asked, “why don’t you work at Notion?”

So, I spent 9 months tracking Notion’s business decisions. I watched the Make with Notion Conference in 2025, attended Notion workshops, and read through hundreds of reviews about their custom agents and workers. 

Then, I whipped up a strategy to boost enterprise custom agent adoption and pitched how I would implement it as an intern. 

2 months of waiting and 120 cold emails later, I’ve made it to San Francisco! The city that rewards running after your wildest obsessions. 

To Kate Rapisarda, Sam Wener, Laura Torrelko, and Laili Attai, I could not be more grateful. Thank you for making my dreams come true. 

To 8-year-old me, irritated about timetables: turns out boring things can lead to living the dream :)

posts.content:
A year ago, we looked at our org design at Notion and saw a gap.
 
We had hired exceptional, high-craft talent. But we didn’t have enough of a bench underneath them. If someone left, we went back to the market. If someone was ready to grow, we didn’t always have the next seat ready. That’s not good enough if you want to build an enduring company.
 
So we made a bet: go big on early career - folks who are curious, AI-native, and have been building their life’s work on Notion since high school. Pair them with our strongest operators. Give them work that drives real business impact. Hold a high bar and build from within.
 
It’s already working in engineering. Grace N. joined us as an intern and picked up a workstream inside our enterprise encryption project that no one handed to her. She saw the need, made the technical calls, and owned the outcome. That work is now what we sell to enterprise customers.
 
Our People team was another first mover. We created an early career pilot program that’s paying dividends. Catherine Seok joined us less than 3 months ago and has built out our PeopleOS, packaging agents that any People team can use out of the box.
 
Now we want to build that muscle across the rest of Notion, which is why we’re hiring our first Head of Early Career Recruiting. We are looking for a leader who is incredibly passionate about the future of work, someone who thrives when guiding candidates at the start of their careers, a leader who gives more energy than they take. Link in comments! 

#lifeatnotion

Last week, I had the pleasure of speaking at Notion's All Hands. I brought two very important things with me: Tate's Bake Shop's tiny cookies and excitement for what we’ve been building alongside the Notion team.

For the past several months, our team has been experimenting with how Agents can make Crafty operate better as we grow.

One thing I shared with the Notion team: the most interesting part hasn’t just been the AI itself, it’s what implementing it forces you to examine.

Where are people spending time they shouldn’t be? Where does knowledge get stuck? Which processes made sense when we were smaller but don’t anymore?
Those questions have led us to rethink work across engineering, operations, onboarding, and more.

Getting to bring some of those lessons directly to the people behind some of the AI tools we use every day was a pretty special full-circle moment. If you haven't tried Notion Custom Agents, I highly recommend you do.

Thank you to the Notion team for having me, and to the Crafty team doing the  building, testing, breaking, fixing, and learning behind everything I got to talk about!

This weekend the Notion community hosted a Notion Market, the first of it's kind globally.

The market featured stall holders who all run their small business on Notion. It was such a lovely event. 

I absolutely love seeing all the unique ways Notion is used, and the market brought out a diverse group of stall holders: flower bouquets, Japanese bagels, ceramics, homewares, matcha, tea, stickers, mochi, live portrait drawing... list goes on. 

It wasn't your typical weekend market. Vanessa Intan curated a series of talks and workshops from the Notion community, covering all topics and sharing how each of them use Notion to help them build their life's work.

Kudos to Vanessa Intan and Alec from Kara's Home who put this incredible market together.

I wish we could do this every month.

posts.content:
i am in awe of Notion's community of creative entrepreneurs 🥹

at last sunday's Notion Market, alongside stuffing my face with crème brûlée mochi, i was so inspired by the stories i heard from the vendors, many building these businesses alongside their 9–5s(!)

some of the awesome people i yapped with (all the way til closing):

𝟭. 𝗟𝘂𝗰𝘆 + 𝗔𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗮 (@𝗰𝗵𝗮𝘄𝘂_𝘁𝗲𝗮) — launched a tea brand from 0→1 in six months alongside full-time jobs: sourcing tea from China, designing packaging, building e-commerce + collaborating with cafés..

𝟮. 𝗟𝗶𝗻𝗴 + 𝗦𝗮𝗿𝗮𝗵 (@𝘆𝘂𝗹𝗶.𝗸𝗶𝗹𝗻) — work besties whose ceramics and print business started with: “gurl wtf you’re so talented at your craft” → “wait… should we start a business together?” 

𝟯. 𝗔𝗻𝗻𝗮 + 𝗘𝗿𝘃𝗶𝗻 (@𝗰𝗵𝗮𝘆𝘂𝘂.𝗺𝗮𝘁𝗰𝗵𝗮) — crème brûlée matcha(!!). also a serendipitous reunion: i hadn’t seen Ervin Zhou since we volunteered together at uni eight years ago. i was stoked when he said: “i’m running a stall here!”

𝟰. 𝗝𝗲𝘀𝘀 (@𝗽𝗹𝗮𝗻𝗻𝗲𝗱𝗯𝘆𝗷𝘆𝘀𝗹𝗮) — left engineering and has been building her sticker + journalling business full-time for seven years (!).

𝟱. 𝗦𝗶𝗼𝗯𝗮𝗵𝗻 (@𝗽𝗹𝗮𝗶𝗻.𝗿𝗶𝗰𝗲.𝘀𝘁𝘂𝗱𝗶𝗼𝘀) — recently took a career break to go give art + acting a real shot. i'm so bullish.

watching them light up as they talked about their creations and the people supporting them made my heart so warm. putting art into the world takes courage. turning it into a business takes grit + perseverance.

a few things i’m taking away:

𝟭/ 𝗴𝗼 𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗼𝗳 𝘆𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝘄𝗮𝘆 𝘁𝗼 𝘀𝘂𝗿𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 𝘆𝗼𝘂𝗿𝘀𝗲𝗹𝗳 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝗽𝗲𝗼𝗽𝗹𝗲 𝘄𝗵𝗼 𝗶𝗻𝘀𝗽𝗶𝗿𝗲 𝘆𝗼𝘂 🪄

our creative courage is shaped by the rooms we put ourselves in. in australia, there countless incredible communities of creative builders (Blackbird and arrayah are two i've benefitted enormously from). embed yourselves in them. the ripple effects can be enormous, where ideas can go ideas →sidequests →actual businesses. 

𝟮/ 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗲’𝘀 𝗻𝗼 “𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁” 𝗮𝗻𝘀𝘄𝗲𝗿 𝘁𝗼 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝘆𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘃𝘀 𝗹𝗲𝗮𝘃𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗽𝗼𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲 👩🏻‍💻

don't let anyone convince you otherwise. 

𝟯/ 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗹𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗹 𝗼𝗳 𝘄𝗵𝗶𝗺𝘀𝘆 𝗶𝗻 𝗮𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗹𝗶𝗮'𝘀 𝘁𝗲𝗰𝗵 𝘀𝗰𝗲𝗻𝗲 𝗶𝘀 𝗮𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝘁𝗼 𝗲𝘅𝗽𝗹𝗼𝗱𝗲 🦄

the overflowing waitlist for the Notion Market says something: people want more experiences like this. people want places where ideas and creatives can collide and scheme and be magnets for eachother.

~ 

huge congrats to Vanessa Intan, Alec from Kara's Home, all the vendors/ speakers/ volunteers and the Notion team behind the scenes Louisa McSpedden, Caroline Huynh, Sophie Mckay, and Emma Yee Yick. the market (first notion event of its kind!) imo was a raging success 😎

~

For most small businesses, figuring out where AI can be useful is just one more job alongside everything else they’re juggling.

Last week, I partnered with Notion to make space for that conversation. We hosted a coffee cupping with a small group of owners + operators from San Francisco’s coffee industry.

The spectrum was pretty wide -- a couple roasters had already built complex workflows for their businesses, while other operators were just getting started. We spent time discussing real workflows + challenges around inventory, taxes, logistics and quality control.

We built one of these workflows live with Mitchell from Coffee Movement, using Notion AI to turn their inventory data into a weekly delivery list.

This is the first in a series of conversations we’re hoping to have with small-business owners about how technology can support their work.

If you run a small business and there’s a workflow you wish took less time, we’d love to hear about it!
